purpose: Teach: 買わ/積ん/はいる/移る/直っ/治り/片付ける/歩ける

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、お父さん、若い頃、買わない物を決めてたぞ、覚えてる?
lines.en: Grandma — do you remember when your father wouldn't buy certain things on purpose back then?
lines.style: Soft, searching tone. Pause before the question—almost half-asking himself. Warm nostalgia with a note of tenderness. Let the memory live in the silence.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。お祖父ちゃん、本を積んでお読みになったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes — your grandfather would stack up those books and read them, wouldn't he, dear?
lines.style: Gently correcting, meeting him in the memory. Voice lifts slightly at 'wouldn't he'—inviting him back into the shared recollection. Intimate and present.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、お部屋にはいると笑顔だったぞ、覚えてる?
lines.en: Grandma — when he'd come into the room, his whole face would light up. You remember that?
lines.style: Quieter now, more specific. The wonder still lives in his voice. He's painting the image as he speaks—letting her see it again through his eyes.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、新しい家に移る時、緊張されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather was so nervous when we moved into the new house, wasn't he, dear?
lines.style: Gentle affirmation with a knowing smile in the voice. She's adding her own detail—softly confirming what he's drawn out. No condescension, just recognition.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、お父さんの怪我、直って嬉しかったぞ、覚えてる?
lines.en: Grandma — I remember being so happy when your father's injury finally healed. Do you?
lines.style: The relief surfaces in his voice now, not just the memory. He's reliving that small joy. Breathier, lighter—the weight lifted from that old worry.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃんの治り、早かったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather recovered so quickly though, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Quick, bright—almost surprised by the recollection. A moment of pride in him slips through. Voice warm but brisk, practical pride wrapped in affection.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、お庭を片付けるのお得意だったぞ、覚えてる?
lines.en: Grandma — you were so good at tidying up the garden. Do you remember?
lines.style: Admiration clear in his tone. A slight smile—he's picturing her at work. Slower pace to let the image settle. Pride in what she could do.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、歩ける距離、お散歩されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather would take such long walks, wouldn't he, dear?
lines.style: A note of wistfulness—those walks are part of what they both miss now. Voice settles, slower. The affection is very close to the surface here.
